title: Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases: Schedule of Case Plans, Opening Records and Case Conditions
content:
Every Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases case is held under one of six case plans. The plan is fixed by the maturity event the case is opened for, and the plan's settings below govern the case while it is open.

## Schedule A: the event each plan covers and the record that opens it

| Case plan | Applies when | Record that opens the case | Date taken as the event date |
|---|---|---|---|
| Death of Last Surviving Borrower | no borrower on the loan is living | an accepted death notice with a death certificate | the date of death |
| Sale or Title Transfer | title has passed to someone who is not a borrower | a recorded deed | the deed recording date |
| Extended Health-Care Absence | non-occupancy was confirmed because the health-care absence limit was exceeded | the occupancy profile showing the health-care absence limit exceeded | the non-occupancy date |
| Principal Residence Change | non-occupancy was confirmed because the home is no longer the principal residence | the occupancy profile showing confirmed non-occupancy | the non-occupancy date |
| Property Charge Default | the property charge repayment arrangement is not in good standing | an unrepaid property-charge advance referred for non-payment | the date of the first unrepaid advance |
| Property Condition Default | a condition inspection has failed | a failed condition inspection report | the condition inspection date |

Under every plan, the date the servicer learns of the event (the case's opened date) is the date the documentation was received.

## Schedule B: case conditions by plan

| Case plan | Vacant-property inspection ordered within | Vacant property may be secured | Condition inspection report must be on file |
|---|---|---|---|
| Death of Last Surviving Borrower | 30 calendar days of opening | yes | no |
| Sale or Title Transfer | 0 (none ordered; the property is normally occupied) | no | no |
| Extended Health-Care Absence | 30 calendar days of opening | yes | no |
| Principal Residence Change | 30 calendar days of opening | yes | no |
| Property Charge Default | 0 (none ordered) | no | no |
| Property Condition Default | 0 (none ordered) | yes | yes |

The following settings are the same under all six plans:

- **Loan programs covered:** HECM loans and Cedarline Summit loans.
- **Loan disbursements suspended while the case is open:** yes.
- **Interest, MIP and servicing fees keep accruing during the case:** yes.
- **Scheduled review of an open case:** every 30 calendar days.
- **Statuses in which a case counts as open:** opened, awaiting HUD approval, deferred, due and payable, extension period, foreclosure referred.
- **Transfer into a revocable living trust in which a borrower keeps occupancy and a life interest counts as a sale or transfer:** no.
- **Transfer between borrowers on the note counts as a sale or transfer:** no.

## Schedule C: order of precedence among maturity events (highest first)

1. Death of Last Surviving Borrower
2. Sale or Title Transfer
3. Principal Residence Change
4. Extended Health-Care Absence
5. Property Condition Default
6. Property Charge Default

The same order applies under every plan.

## Reading the schedule

*Which plan names a vacant-property inspection with no window?* Sale or Title Transfer, Property Charge Default and Property Condition Default show 0, which means no vacant-property inspection is ordered under those plans.

*Does a case that is cured or resolved still count as open?* No. Only the six statuses listed above count as open.
